of the #136130-related fix from dotnet/runtime#133542 to release/10.0

Fixes Issue dotnet/runtime#136130

main PR https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/133542

# Description

<!-- Give a brief summary of the issue and how the pull request is fixing it. -->

When folding a complement of an AVX packed compare, the JIT now writes the inverted comparison mode to the immediate. This preserves `Avx.AndNot(Avx.Compare(...), x)` semantics for the affected modes.

# Customer Impact

<!-- What is the impact to customers of not taking this fix? -->

- [x] Customer reported
- [ ] Found internally

The report describes incorrect vector results in optimized .NET 10 x64 code with AVX2 for four comparison modes. A source-level workaround exists, but it requires changing the application expression or comparison mode.

# Regression

<!-- Is this fixing a problem that was introduced in the most recent release, ie., fixing a regression? -->

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No

The report states that .NET 8 produces correct results and .NET 10.0.13 does not; the exact introducing change has not been identified.

# Testing

<!-- What kind of testing has been done with the fix. -->

Added a focused JIT regression test for all four affected comparison modes, including an unordered NaN lane. CI will validate the `release/10.0` build and run the test.

# Risk

<!-- Please assess the risk of taking this fix. Provide details backing up your assessment. -->

Low. The change writes the already-computed inverse predicate instead of the original predicate; the regression test covers the reported modes. The target is `release/10.0`, as required for .NET 10 and later servicing branches.

# Package authoring no longer needed in .NET 9

IMPORTANT: Starting with .NET 9, you no longer need to edit a NuGet package's csproj to enable building and bump the version.
Keep in mind that we still need package authoring in .NET 8 and older versions.

Resolves dotnet/runtime#136130
